import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a clean style for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a categorical plot (box plot) to visualize price distribution
# It shows price by sensor type, with hue for 4K video capability,
# and separated into columns by body type to allow for multi-faceted comparison.
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x='sensor_type',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='has_video_4k',
    col='body_type',  # Create separate columns for each body_type
    kind='box',       # Use box plot to show distributions
    palette='viridis',
    height=5,         # Height of each facet
    aspect=1.2,       # Aspect ratio of each facet
    col_wrap=2,       # Wrap columns after 2 plots if there are many body types
    legend=False      # Disable automatic legend to add a custom one later
)

# Add an overall title to the figure
g.fig.suptitle('Camera Price Distribution by Sensor Type, 4K Video, and Body Type', y=1.02, fontsize=16)

# Improve x-axis labels for readability across all facets
for ax in g.axes.flat:
    ax.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45, ha='right')
    ax.set_xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=10) # Set x-label for each subplot

# Set y-axis label for the entire figure
g.set_ylabels('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Create custom legend for the 'has_video_4k' hue
# Define labels for 0 and 1 values of 'has_video_4k'
legend_labels = {0: 'No 4K Video', 1: 'Has 4K Video'}
# Get unique values from the 'has_video_4k' column, sorted to match palette order
hue_values = sorted(df['has_video_4k'].unique())
# Create proxy artists for the legend using the viridis palette colors
legend_elements = [mpatches.Patch(facecolor=sns.color_palette('viridis')[i], label=legend_labels[val])
                   for i, val in enumerate(hue_values)]

# Add the custom legend to the figure
g.fig.legend(handles=legend_elements, title='4K Video Capability', loc='upper right', bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.9))

# Adjust layout to make room for the legend and prevent labels from overlapping
g.fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1]) # Adjust rect to leave space for the legend on the right

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
